answer: A bonded collateral protocol deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to anchor their public keys to slashable cryptocurrency deposits. An attacker incurs the verifiable financial cost of locking dedicated capital per identity, whether deploying agents to manage telemetry for a citrus grove or settle transactions for a cultured pearl auction. However, this capital lockup creates steep economic barriers for lightweight agents and fails if malicious exploit gains exceed the slashed stake.
